record.title_md: Covering powers of cycles with equivalence subgraphs

dossier_meta.catalog_title: Covering powers of cycles with equivalence subgraphs
dossier_meta.subject: Graph Theory
dossier_meta.statement_text: Conjecture Given $ k $ and $ n $ , the graph $ C_{n}^k $ has equivalence covering number $ \Omega(k) $ .
dossier_meta.context_text: Given a graph $ G $ , a subgraph $ H $ of $ G $ is an equivalence subgraph of $ G $ if $ H $ a disjoint union of cliques. The quivalence covering number of $ G $ , denoted $ eq(G) $ , is the least number of equivalence subgraphs needed to cover the edges of $ G $ . This problem has been studied by various people since the 80s [A]. For line graphs, the equivalence covering number is known to within a constant factor [EGK]. It is therefore tempting to examine the situation for quasi-line graphs and claw-free graphs. Powers of cycles are perhaps the simplest interesting class of claw-free graphs that are not necessarily line graphs. However, even for $ n $ very large compared to $ k $ , no upper bound is known beyond trivial linear bounds of order $ \Theta(k) $ . Furthermore, it is not even certain that a nontrivial lower bound (i.e. going to infinity as $ k $ goes to infinity) is known. It is possible that this can be related somehow to a known result, but for now it seems at least superficially that this problem is wide open.
dossier_meta.references_text:
- [A] N. Alon, Covering graphs with the minimum number of equivalence relations, Combinatorica 6 (1986) 201–206.
- [EGK] L. Esperet, J. Gimbel, A. King, Covering line graphs with equivalence relations, Discrete Applied Mathematics Volume 158, Issue 17, 28 October 2010, Pages 1902-1907.
